scope_findings.claim: Fellowship type is European Fellowship (EF) with a 24-month duration hosted in an EU Member State (Hungary). Duration is within the 12–24 month permitted range for European Postdoctoral Fellowships.

The researcher undertakes intra-EU international mobility from Bulgaria (Plovdiv University 'Paisii Hilendarski') to Hungary (ELTE), qualifying as an experienced postdoctoral researcher undertaking international mobility as an excellent researcher.
The host institution is Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest, Hungary — a higher education establishment in an EU Member State satisfying the European Fellowship host-country requirement.
The application is made jointly by the researcher (Dr. Mariya Petrova) and an academic-sector beneficiary (ELTE).

A Career Development Plan is established jointly by the supervisor (Prof. Dr. Gábor Nagy) and the fellow, submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action (by months 2–3), and reviewed and updated at M12 and M24. The plan covers research objectives, training needs, transferable skills, publications, career development milestones (≥3 peer-reviewed publications, ≥120 hours transferable-skills training, MSc co-supervision, follow-on proposal within 6 months of fellowship end), and participation in open-science events.

Training integrates digital and AI skills including responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding, knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship (translating the uncertainty-aware decision-support demonstrator toward user uptake), and research integrity and open-science ethics (FAIR data management, open research software, reproducible validation protocols).

The fellowship prepares the researcher for digital collaboration, FAIR data management, and societal engagement including stakeholder engagement with the farming community through an associated partner (AgroVIR Kft.) providing farmer access and field feedback.

The research topic is uncertainty-aware multi-sensor crop/soil/water diagnosis and economically optimised irrigation decision support for row crops (horticulture), including crop water stress monitoring, root-zone soil moisture estimation, and profit-based irrigation recommendation using Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, PlanetScope high-resolution imagery, in-situ soil sensors, and weather data.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element directly affirms or excludes this research domain. MSCA-PF scope requirements (SR-01 through SR-09) define fellowship structural and procedural requirements without restricting research topics; no requirement_id in scope_requirements.json positively maps to this research domain. The call's thematic openness cannot be confirmed from Tier 2B data alone and cannot be relied upon as generic programme knowledge per CLAUDE.md §13.9. Scope boundary is defined by Tier 2B only.

scope_findings.claim: The methodological design employs two interchangeable diagnostic routes — Route A (Direct Probabilistic Fusion: satellite imagery as covariate alongside SAR, optical, weather, soil sensors in a Bayesian hierarchical model or Gaussian process yielding distributional field-state estimates) and Route B (Homogeneous Patch Proxy: a nearby covarying patch cleanly readable by the coarse pixel) — sharing a single AquaCrop-based uncertainty-aware decision engine with end-to-end uncertainty propagation from observation to irrigation decision.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element affirms or excludes this methodological framework or the specific technologies employed (AquaCrop, Bayesian hierarchical models, Gaussian processes, Sentinel-1/2, PlanetScope, counterfactual irrigation simulation). MSCA-PF scope requirements do not define thematic or methodological scope restrictions. Flagged as no positive Tier 2B mapping exists; scope boundary is defined by Tier 2B only.

scope_findings.claim: The scientific novelty is the end-to-end coupling of learned multimodal fusion, explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation, and economically optimised irrigation decision, argued against a systematic literature review identifying this combination as underdeveloped for row crops.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element affirms or excludes this novelty claim or the research literature gap it references. MSCA-PF scope requirements do not define topic-level or novelty-domain scope restrictions. Flagged as no positive Tier 2B mapping exists; scope boundary is defined by Tier 2B only.

scope_findings.claim: The tool is presented as a standalone research demonstrator (MVP) rather than a product, with validation requiring a protocol covering ground-truth collection, uncertainty calibration assessment (e.g. whether 90% prediction intervals contain truth ~90% of the time), and pilot success criteria.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element affirms or excludes the research-demonstrator framing or the specific validation protocol design for this instrument. MSCA-PF scope requirements do not define TRL targets or output-type restrictions. Flagged as no positive Tier 2B mapping exists; scope boundary is defined by Tier 2B only.

scope_findings.claim: AgroVIR Kft. (Hungary) is included as an associated partner providing farmer access, field validation, and feedback; it is explicitly described as not owning or operating the research tool.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element directly addresses the role of an associated partner providing field-validation access. CC-07 and CC-08 govern non-academic placements at the end of the project, a distinct structural mechanism that does not apply to AgroVIR's described validation-access role. The associated partner arrangement has no direct mapping in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json. Flagged for operator review to confirm the arrangement does not implicitly invoke non-academic placement constraints (CC-07, CC-08, CC-09) or require additional disclosure under admissibility conditions (CC-15).

scope_findings.claim: The host institution (ELTE, Budapest, Hungary) is located in Hungary, a Horizon Europe widening country. The concept note, strategic positioning, and project summary do not address ERA Fellowship provisions (SR-09, CC-14) or widening participation support under Work Programme Annex 11.
scope_findings.flag_reason: SR-09 and CC-14 describe ERA Fellowships providing specific support for researchers undertaking fellowships in widening countries to support balanced brain circulation. Hungary is a widening country under Horizon Europe. The concept note, strategic positioning, and project summary do not address whether ERA Fellowship provisions (Work Programme Annex 11) apply to this submission or are being sought. Resolution required: operator should confirm whether the ERA Fellowship track applies and, if so, ensure the proposal addresses widening participation and balanced brain circulation as part of the submission.
